instructor:
Dr. Fatih İnci delivered the MSN 512 – Biomedical Materials course in an engaging and highly interactive manner. His comprehensive coverage of topics such as surface chemistry, biosensors, and microfluidic systems significantly broadened our perspective on the field of biomaterials. He frequently used a question-and-answer approach to involve students during lectures, offered clear explanations when needed, and created a supportive and motivating classroom environment.

On the other hand, the expectations surrounding the term project were quite high. Students were asked to prepare a detailed project proposal and deliver a presentation. Given the already intensive course content throughout the semester, this level of workload made time management particularly challenging for many students. A more simplified or earlier-guided project format could have made the process more manageable and effective. Additionally, it was occasionally difficult to hear him clearly during the lectures. Using a microphone could help ensure that all students can follow along comfortably, especially in longer sessions.

Overall, I appreciated Dr. İnci’s teaching approach and his command of the subject matter. Although the course was demanding, it was highly educational and inspiring.
course: From my perspective, the strongest aspect of the course was its broad coverage of topics, which allowed us to approach the field of biomedical materials from multiple angles. Subjects like surface chemistry, biosensors, and microfluidic systems were presented with both theoretical depth and up-to-date content, which really increased my interest in the material. The interactive teaching style and the relaxed, supportive atmosphere created by the instructor also contributed positively to the learning experience. The weakest part of the course was the extensive scope of the term project. Writing a detailed proposal and presenting it, on top of the existing workload from other courses, was quite overwhelming. Additionally, for such an application-oriented subject, I believe more laboratory support would have been beneficial. It would have been extremely valuable to see topics like biosensors, microfluidic systems, and microneedle technologies demonstrated in a hands-on lab setting. Including a dedicated lab component to the course could significantly enhance the overall learning experience.
assistant: There was a teaching assistant (Dilşad) assigned to the course. However, I personally felt that she was not sufficiently prepared or knowledgeable in the subject matter. During paper discussions led by the TA, it became clear that she had limited familiarity with the topics, often stating that her background was in engineering and that she wasn’t fully comfortable with biomedical or biology content. While I understand and appreciate the multidisciplinary nature of the course, I believe that a TA supporting such a content-heavy and complex course should be more familiar with the material or at least put in the effort to compensate for gaps in their background. Stronger preparation and engagement from the assistant would have made the discussion sessions more productive and informative.
